newsitem.title: CHINA: China extends grace period on equipment imports.
newsitem.headline: China extends grace period on equipment imports.

text.p: China has extended until the end of this year the grace period for duty-free imports of capital equipment on some foreign-invested projects of up to $30 million, state television said on Tuesday.
It said the decision, taken by the State Council, or cabinet, applies to those projects that gain final clearance by authorities this year.

Television said the projects had to have been reviewed by central government agencies such as the State Planning Commission, the State Economic and Trade Commission or the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation by April 1, 1996.
China abolished duty-free treatment for imports of capital equipment under sweeping tax revisions that were announced in late 1995 and put into effect on April 1, 1996.
A grace period was originally allowed until the end of last year but further extensions were granted.

In February, the China Business Daily reported that ventures with investments of less than $30 million would be allowed duty-free imports until the end of June this year. Projects worth more than $30 million would be allowed duty-free imports until the end of June 1998.
State television made no mention of projects worth more than $30 million.
